title: Lifted coordinates for a closed immersion of an ample proper fibre
statement: Let $f:Z\to S$ be a proper morphism [def-weil-proper-morphism] of schemes [def-pc-scheme], let $s\in S$, and let $Z_s$ be its scheme-theoretic fibre [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. Assume $S$ is Noetherian, meaning locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]. Let $L$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_Z$-module [def-sc-invertible-module] whose pullback $L_s$ [def-pc-module-pullback] is ample [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module], and assume $Z_s\ne\varnothing$. There exist integers $d\geq1$, $r\geq0$, an affine open neighbourhood $U\subseteq S$ of $s$, and sections $u_0,\ldots,u_r\in\Gamma(Z_U,L^{\otimes d}|_{Z_U})$, where $Z_U=f^{-1}(U)$ and tensor powers are as in [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module], such that their fibre pullbacks $t_j\in\Gamma(Z_s,L_s^{\otimes d})$ generate $L_s^{\otimes d}$ [def-weil-pbc-generating-sections]. The fibre morphism $i_s:Z_s\to\mathbf P^r_{\kappa(s)}$ defined by $(t_0,\ldots,t_r)$ [def-weil-pbc-morphism-to-projective-space-by-sections] is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], with a quotient-compatible isomorphism $i_s^*\mathcal O(1)\cong L_s^{\otimes d}$; here projective space and its twist have the meanings of [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change] and [def-pc-projective-space-twist]. The fibre pullbacks use the natural identification $(L^{\otimes d})|_{Z_s}\cong L_s^{\otimes d}$ of [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor], iterated over the tensor factors, namely the comparison $p_j(L,d)$ of [def-sc-tensor-pullback-power-comparison] for the fibre projection $j:Z_s\to Z$. No generation by the $u_j$ away from $Z_s$ is asserted.

source.place: Tag 0D2N, lemma-ample-in-neighbourhood, first paragraph through lifting all projective coordinates, using lemma-ample-on-fibre.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-ample-fibre-section-lifting] to $f,L,s$ and choose its bound $a$. The fibre structural map $g:Z_s\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ is proper by [lem-pc-proper-base-change](1), hence of finite type by [def-weil-proper-morphism]. The fibre line bundle $L_s$ is invertible by [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor](1) and ample by hypothesis. Apply [lem-trf-affine-eventual-power-immersion] over the field $\kappa(s)$ and choose its bound $b\geq1$. Set $d=\max(a,b)$. That lemma supplies $r\geq0$, an immersion $i:Z_s\to\mathbf P^r_{\kappa(s)}$ over the field, and an isomorphism $\alpha:i^*\mathcal O(1)\xrightarrow{\sim}L_s^{\otimes d}$. In particular $d\geq1$ and the section-lifting lemma applies to every section of this power.

source.place: Tag 0D2N, lemma-ample-in-neighbourhood, first paragraph; Tag 0D2M, lemma-ample-on-fibre; Morphisms Tag 01VT, lemma-finite-type-over-affine-ample-very-ample (1) implies (6).

proof.text: The target $\mathbf P^r_{\kappa(s)}$ is separated over $\kappa(s)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-proj-separated]. Since $i$ is over the field and $g$ is proper, [lem-weil-pbc-proper-to-separated] makes $i$ proper. It is an immersion, so [lem-weil-pbc-proper-immersion-closed] makes it a closed immersion.

source.place: Tag 01W6, lemma-image-proper-scheme-closed; as invoked by Coherent Tag 0D2N. Constructions Tag 01NH (1).

proof.text: Let $T_0,\ldots,T_r$ be the homogeneous coordinate sections and put $t_j=\alpha(i^*T_j)$. In the standard chart $D_+(T_k)$ of [def-nagata-relative-projective-space], the twist of [def-pc-projective-space-twist] has basis $e_k$, and $T_j=(T_j/T_k)e_k$, in particular $T_k=e_k$. These formulas agree with the pullback of the integral projective twist: both have transition $e_l=(T_l/T_k)e_k$. Thus on $i^{-1}D_+(T_k)$ the section $t_k$ is a basis; these opens cover $Z_s$, so the $t_j$ generate in the precise sheaf-surjectivity sense of [def-weil-pbc-generating-sections]. Let $\theta:\mathbf P^r_{\kappa(s)}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbf P(\{0,\ldots,r\};\kappa(s))=\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}\mathbf P^r_{\mathbf Z}$ be the canonical isomorphism over $\kappa(s)$ of [lem-trf-free-projective-bundle-base-change-space]; on the affine base it is the Proj comparison fixing every $T_j$, so $\mathrm{pr}_2\circ\theta$ is given on $D_+(T_k)$ by the coefficient map $\mathbf Z[T]_{(T_k)}\to\kappa(s)[T]_{(T_k)}$ and pulls the integral frames $e_k$ and coordinates $T_j$ back to those of the chart. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-functor-of-points] to $\psi=\mathrm{pr}_2\circ\theta\circ i:Z_s\to\mathbf P^r_{\mathbf Z}$. Its generating pair is exactly $(L_s^{\otimes d},(t_j))$, using the displayed transition formulas and $\alpha$. Uniqueness there and the fibre-product definition of [def-weil-pbc-morphism-to-projective-space-by-sections] (both projections of $\theta\circ i$ agree with $g$ and $\psi$) show that the morphism $i_s$ defined by these sections is $\theta\circ i$; it is a closed immersion by Step 2, since $\theta$ is an isomorphism. The isomorphism $\alpha$ sends every pulled-back coordinate to $t_j$, hence is quotient-compatible.

source.place: Tag 01NE, lemma-projective-space, and the description after Definition 01NF; standard coordinate frames of the twist.

proof.text: For each of the finitely many $j=0,\ldots,r$, use the lifting lemma with this same $d\geq a$ and $t_j$. Obtain $s\in U_j\subseteq S$ and $v_j\in\Gamma(f^{-1}(U_j),L^{\otimes d})$ with fibre pullback $t_j$. Its hypotheses are exactly those of the item and do not require flatness or generation away from the fibre. The comparison used by the lifting statement is the tensor pullback identification of [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor](2); its iterated comparison on $d$ factors is $p_j(L,d)$ of [def-sc-tensor-pullback-power-comparison]. On a tensor of local sections it sends $1\otimes(\ell_1\otimes\cdots\otimes\ell_d)$ to $(1\otimes\ell_1)\otimes\cdots\otimes(1\otimes\ell_d)$, by its recursive definition and the normalized unit $\ell\mapsto1\otimes\ell$. This is precisely the natural identification specified in the item, with no arbitrary scalar rescaling.

source.place: Tag 0D2N, first paragraph, lifting the coordinates via 0D2M; normalized pullback and tensor comparison as specified in the item.

proof.text: The finite intersection $W=\bigcap_{j=0}^r U_j$ is an open neighbourhood of $s$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis], choose an affine open $s\in U\subseteq W$. Restrict $v_j$ to $Z_U=f^{-1}(U)$ and call it $u_j$. Restriction followed by fibre pullback equals the original fibre pullback: on local sections both maps are $v\mapsto1\otimes v$, as in the pullback convention of [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor]. Consequently every $u_j$ pulls back to $t_j$ through the comparison fixed in Step 4. Steps 2 and 3 show that these fibre sections generate and define the closed immersion $i$ with its quotient-compatible twist isomorphism. Together with $d\geq1$, $r\geq0$ and affine $U$, these are all the requested data.
